title: instance.constructor different when .scope() is used to retrieve the instance
author: aforty

comments.body:
`.scope / .unscope` creates a new copy of model, instances created by them refer to this new copy. For identification purpose you can use `instance.constructor.name` which should be common for different scoped instances.

We need a new copy of class to maintain multiple scopes at a time. If we keep the class same, changing scope on one of them will change scope on other sibling classes.

satisfaction_conditions: An explanation of why instance constructors differ when using .scope()
Understanding of the technical reasoning behind Sequelize's scope implementation
A workaround or alternative approach for instance identification

_classification.category: Can be dockerized without any issue

title: Where clause failed on second level nested include
author: mlegenhausen

comments.body:
The problem is the subquery, have you tested this against master? A fix was introduced in something similar to this.

Else try adding required: true to child1, or required: false to both child1 and child2

Tested against master with same result as before.

Adding `required:false` to  `child2` did the trick (with dev11 and master).
Yeah `required: false` will turn off the subquery since it doesn't need to be there anymore - I guess there's an issue with having a required :M child to a non required parent.
Thanks that saved my day again :) Great project and great maintainers!
This solves the problem of the query error, but if I use it the where clause no longer constrains the query. I need both. Is there any work around to this other than doing two separate queries?

title: `include` breaks when using `include: { daoFactory: DaoFactory1, as: 'factory' }` form
body:
Not sure if it has to do with the association in my db being backwards.

I have 

```
Address.hasOne(Firm);
Company.belongsTo(Address);
```

This works as expected:  

```
Company.findAll({include: [Address]});
```

But this breaks:  

```
Company.findAll({include: [{daoFactory: Address, as: 'address'}]});  
```

author: cheapsteak

comments.body:
The `as` option is only for when you have explicitly aliased your relation, like this:

``` js
Company.belongsTo(Address, { as: 'HomeAddress' })

Company.findAll({include: [{model: Address, as: 'HomeAddress'}]});  
```
If your association is using `as` you need to use it in your `include` statement aswell.

```
Address.hasOne(Firm, { as: 'Company'} );
Company.belongsTo(Address, { as: 'Address', foreignKey: 'address_id'});  //added explicit alias

Company.findAll({  //same as before
  where: { compay_ids : ids },
  include: [{model: Address, as: 'Address'}]
})  
```

Or remove the alias all together. But you have to pick one, no alias, or alias on both.
Put another way, you can only use `as` in include if you also use `as` in the association. It is not possible to load your model under another name when including
Ah, I see. Thank you for the clarification. That worked.
A continuing point of confusion, guess we'll have to clear up the docs on that somehow.

Working example of the correct syntax for including associated models with aliases
